text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: cross-region routing anomaly detected. Significant portion of requests from us-east are being routed via eu-west. Latency spike observed (p50 ~850ms, usual p50 ~120ms). Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging @oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: got the page, joining. are we seeing errors or just latency?

alex: mostly latency and a small increase in 5xxs (0.6% -> 1.8%). traces show long network hop times, traceroute from edge -> eu-west transit.

priya: looks like an unintended routing policy change rolled out 3m ago. I can see a config diff: `route.priority = region-agnostic` applied to the global policy.

maria: are we sure it's config and not cloud-level control plane issue? cloud provider reported an AZ fabric flapping event in eu-west-last-hour but they said it was resolved.

kevin: checking BGP/transit tables now. early glance: some announced paths for us-east prefixes point to eu-west transit for a subset of POPs.

incident-bot: Pager: mitigation runbook suggested: 1) add temporary route pin for affected customer prefixes 2) rollback recent global policy 3) update status page.

oncall-sre: I'm going to apply a temporary pin to force us-east steering for production prefixes. Using internal CLI:
```
rwctl routing override --scope prefixes --prefixes @prod_us --region us-east --ttl 60 --reason "emergency pin: cross-region leak"
```

alex: ack. running now.

alex: applied override to 8 POPs. monitoring latency.

priya: rolling back the `region-agnostic` change in policy repo now. diff: revert commit c3f9a2.

maria: cloud provider confirms their fabric is stable now but they saw some propagation delay across regions which could explain transient BGP path selection.

support-ops: do we have customer impact list? CS already getting pings from 2 enterprise customers reporting timeouts.

kevin: routing metrics show successful shift back to us-east within ~90s after override. p50 dropped to 140ms, errors back to baseline.

oncall-sre: good. marking mitigation as applied. Next: evaluate if we should increase TTL for override while we investigate root cause. Thoughts?

priya: set ttl to 300s for now. we need a postmortem to understand why policy rollout allowed region-agnostic to leak. maybe a missing validation test in CI.

alex: changed TTL.\\n
incident-bot: Status update suggestion: "Partial latency degradation affecting US customers between 16:12–16:15 UTC due to cross-region routing policy change. Mitigation applied 16:15 UTC (temporary route pin)." Want me to post to status.redwood.ai?

support-ops: please post and note affected orgs: AcmeCorp, BrightCloud — both reported issues. Add link to this thread.

maria: I'm opening a ticket with cloud NOC to request historical BGP propagation logs for the window 16:00–16:20 UTC.

kevin: saving relevant routing snapshots and traceroutes to incident artifact bucket: s3://incidents/1768452001/

oncall-sre: assigning postmortem owner: @priya. please include CI gating for routing-policy changes and a canary rollout step.

priya: taking ownership. will schedule a follow-up postmortem meeting.

alex: retro note: our rollout tooling allowed a global flag flip without traffic steering canary. need to add a safety check.

incident-bot: Incident severity proposed: Sev2 (partial user impact). Candidate updates: timeline, mitigation actions, customer impact, follow-ups gathered.

support-ops: contacting affected customers with an incident note and ETA for postmortem.

priya: creating the postmortem doc now: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/1768452001 (placeholder).

oncall-sre: leaving handoff notes: mitigation in place (override ttl 300s), metrics stable for 8m, rollback of policy completed. if latency returns, escalate to network infra and cloud NOC.

maria: thanks team. great quick response. :thumbsup:

kevin: will keep monitoring for another 30m and then we can remove temporary override and rely on fixed policy once we have confidence.

incident-bot: Auto-note: paging resolved for @oncall-sre at 16:20 UTC. If no regressions, incident will be closed to monitoring in 60m.
